steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Molly, you've lost so much weight!

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: I did spend two whole months in bed.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I went looking for you once the plate stopped. When I saw medics carrying you out all covered in blood, and you weren't moving, I thought you were dead...

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: His singing voice is... terrifying.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: But he only wanted to stop me. He didn't want to kill me.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: It definitely wasn't a coincidence that he bumped into Greta at the auction, like she said. He had another motive to join the film crew.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: And what was that?

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: He was looking for something that exists, something that's always with us, even though we know nothing about it.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Okay... I knew he was a mysterious dude, but now I'm even more confused.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: But forget about him!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I'm sorry for taking so long to come see you. Mostly because they make it a real pain to file a visitation application for this place.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: I know, Tippi.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: But I used you and caused others to misunderstand you...

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Lucian was right. I was ignoring the truth in my hands. In my final moments of madness, I didn't even... think of you...

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Listen to me, Molly.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: No matter what you went through, no matter what your goal, you hurt the people who were by our side practically twenty-four seven. You're a criminal, and I won't ever forgive you for that!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: ...But that doesn't mean I can't also miss the times we would crash on the sofa to watch horror flicks, just the two of us.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Wasn't that fun? Wasn't that, like, real?

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: ...Yeah.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: When I was stuck in bed, my wounds hurt so bad I couldn't sleep. I kept recalling everything that happened...

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: A whole night would pass, but only my pain was real.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Honestly, it doesn't matter how absurd a story gets, or if we're all puppets of fate or whatever. It's not like I never had a choice.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: If only I'd focused more on the movies we were watching, instead of thinking about the truth I thought was real—hatred, madness, blood, and puppets.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: I'm sorry, Tippi.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: If I'd met you earlier, maybe you wouldn't have even needed 'Laura'.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: The final day of your trial's in two days, right? I talked to a few lawyers, and it seems like...

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Don't let my ending bother you.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: The warden's nice here. He let me stay in the prison's logistics department during these last few days, to make stuff the prisoners can use.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: I'm not living like I was before, merely waiting in vain for the finale.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Good, good.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Haha, you're almost out of visiting time, so let's talk about happier stuff.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: What happened to the movie we all shot together?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Wow, everyone's here already! Sorry I'm late!

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Nervous, Steven?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: A bit.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Relax.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: We shot that ridiculous finale, and then it went to editing, color grading, and music production... Everyone did their best to complete production in only two months.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: I'm glad we agreed on the title change, Steven.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: I should be thanking you again for your final performance inside the Catastrophe. Otherwise, deleting those three words would've been nothing but pretentious navel-gazing.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Lady Dupont is by no means as attention-grabbing as The Death of Lady Dupont, but let Greta worry about the marketing... There is no doubt in my mind that our new title suits the story best.

spans.text: is by no means as attention-grabbing as
, but let Greta worry about the marketing... There is no doubt in my mind that our new title suits the story best.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Right, I'll handle it.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: I'll get Lady Dupont into theaters...

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: then visit a police station to do what I have to do.

steps.name: Excited Reporter A
steps.text: Pinch me. I'm not seeing things, am I?

steps.name: Excited Reporter B
steps.text: Pinch you? Just snap your shutter already! This is guaranteed to go on the front page tomorrow!

steps.name: Excited Reporter B
steps.text: How did the niche AGFF attract such a distinguished guest? How much did the organizers spend?

steps.name: Excited Reporter A
steps.text: How many years has it been since Marianne Blake showed up in Wrankwood?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Grandma Jara!

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: It's been a while, Tip.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Judging by your outfit... let me guess what your role in this was. Script supervisor? Prop master? Stuntwoman? Or some kind of 'Furniture City Warrior'?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Background painter, of course!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I've been in this crew for half a year, and was even selected to join the Wrankwood studio plate restoration project last week!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: The plate our crew rented got totally wrecked by the Catastrophe, so the boss put me in charge of the design work once it's rebuilt, and I've been, like, soooo busy...

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Haha, I see you've finally figured out what you want to do.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I told you before, didn't I? I love movies, every last part of them!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: And now, I finally found out what my favorite part is!

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: So, you don't plan on going back?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Hehe, think you could keep shielding me from the old man?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Tip, your grandfather may be an old friend of mine who used to be my finest partner in the industry, but that doesn't mean he'll let me tell him how to raise his grandkids.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Just tell him this the next time you have tea with him:

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Ahem—

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: 'We're all retired, aren't we, old chap? Why waste our time worrying about the little things?'

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: 'I know Tip didn't use any of your contacts, nor did she follow your plan to become a historical film director, but isn't she living it up in Wrankwood?'

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: 'Who knows, half the backdrops in town might be spray-painted by your granddaughter one day!'

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Alright, I recorded all that. I'll play it for him the next time we meet.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: ...Aw, Grandma Jara!

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Fine, fine. But I might not have the time to see your grandpa the next time I'm in Columbia.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Oh yeah, didn't you go all the way to Rim Billiton for some fresh air? Did you come back for Rhine Lab stuff?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: That's too many questions, Tip.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Once the screening's done, I have to head over to Max D.C. to see the vice president…

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: So at least let me have a chat with an old friend, will you?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Long time no see, Marianne.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Just call me Jara.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: After so many years away from the silver screen, 'Marianne' sounds like a stranger's name to me.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Either way, I have to thank you... Jara.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: I'm sure you know that given my current reputation, I don't have much of an influence in the industry anymore.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: So without your help, the AGFF would never have allowed Lady Dupont as a late submission.

spans.text: So without your help, the AGFF would never have allowed

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: It was my pleasure.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Though, I must say, I had no idea that Tippi was actually—

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: I would have helped you with or without her.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: I just watched the part with the Catastrophe, and felt it'd be such a pity for the audience to miss out on the actress's performance. So I thought I'd do an old friend a favor.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: But even if Lady Dupont gets free marketing at AGFF, that doesn't always translate into box office numbers.

spans.text: gets free marketing at AGFF, that doesn't always translate into box office numbers.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Melanie, you know better than I that if Wrankwood were a person, he would be the most forgetful and least-tolerant person there is.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: ...It's no guarantee that he'd accept a lover running back into his arms.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Besides, you did destroy an entire plate. Even if the film's a smash hit, you might not make enough to pay for the damages.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: At least I did it. And I have no regrets.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: But rather than mulling over all that, I'd like to... ask you a question.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Go ahead.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: When you encountered a Catastrophe while shooting The Eternally Shining Star, the camera caught you as the storm nearly missed you...

spans.text: When you encountered a Catastrophe while shooting
, the camera caught you as the storm nearly missed you...

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Was it just an accident, like you said at the press conference, or...

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Did you also move toward it of your own will?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Is the answer to that still important to you, even now?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: Hahahaha. No.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: *sigh* It sure is hard to say if I really did beat you in the end!
The splendidly dressed female lead laughs heartily before every camera in the room, though she does not even know what she is laughing at.

After a long time, she opens her arms towards her former rival, the genius she always thought she would never catch up to, the one she had always exchanged polite greetings with on camera, for a hug...
And it is returned in kind.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Let's head in.

a.text: Art Department   Carl, Bob, Tippi, Jericho...

steps.name: Audience Member A
steps.text: ...It's over?

steps.name: Audience Member B
steps.text: Yup.

steps.name: Audience Member A
steps.text: Thoughts on the film?

steps.name: Audience Member B
steps.text: I heard about what happened behind the scenes—the murders, the Catastrophe, even the project management was a mess.

steps.name: Audience Member B
steps.text: So before I sat down to watch it, I thought the film couldn't possibly live up to all that. But...

steps.name: Audience Member B
steps.text: An absurd noble's marriage breakdown ending with a Catastrophe—the plot twists made sense, but so many of the characters were just bizarre...

steps.name: Audience Member B
steps.text: It's hard to say if it's good or bad, but it's a lot to chew on.

steps.name: Audience Member A
steps.text: Same, to be honest.

steps.name: Audience Member A
steps.text: Story aside, even the production was pretty controversial. Like, the cinematography is inconsistent at times...

steps.name: Audience Member A
steps.text: The first part was shot meticulously like a serious historical drama, but it becomes rougher and rougher towards the end, especially the Catastrophe scenes, where it's totally filmed like a documentary!

steps.name: Audience Member A
steps.text: It's definitely going to be polarizing. The fans will rate it highly, while the haters are going to hate it.

spans.text: It's definitely going to be polarizing. The fans will rate it highly, while the haters are going to

steps.name: Audience Member B
steps.text: But that's what makes it interesting, isn't it?

steps.name: Audience Member B
steps.text: Wrankwood's been getting more and more boring over the years, and that goes for AGFF films too...

steps.name: Audience Member B
steps.text: But this one? I'd buy a ticket to Lady Dupont.

spans.text: But this one? I'd buy a ticket to

steps.name: Audience Member A
steps.text: Let's see what the director and cast have to say during the post-screening round table.

steps.name: Audience Member A
steps.text: Oh yeah, I heard that unlucky-looking gal in the front worked on it too...

steps.name: Hautin
steps.text: Hoo boy... My luck is awful.

steps.name: Hautin
steps.text: After a month of applications, I finally landed a spot as their last stagehand, but then all of that happened the moment I arrived on set. I lost so much sleep after running into those corpses...

spans.text: After a month of applications, I finally landed a spot as their last stagehand, but then all of
happened the moment I arrived on set. I lost so much sleep after running into those corpses...

steps.name: Hautin
steps.text: And if it weren't for the insomnia, I wouldn't have kicked the wall with my mind all messed up, and broken my leg when I was trying to follow everyone down to safety when the Catastrophe came near...

steps.name: Hautin
steps.text: And if I didn't break my leg, I wouldn't have missed my bus and missed the first half of the screening...
The unlucky stagehand mutters to herself as the credits roll. She recalls her experience and cannot help but feel sorrowful about it all.
Even the images on the screen feel strange to her. The familiar faces and scenes have all been assembled in a way she cannot understand...
Just like her 'topsy-turvy' life.
Then, she spots her name at the end of the credits.

steps.name: Hautin
steps.text: 'Stage Department: Hautin'...
No matter how the hand of fate may change, it will eventually leave a line, a truth you believe in.

steps.name: Playwright
steps.text: It's over. Aren't you taking part in the post-screening round table?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: I'm not with them. Besides... the two of you are here.

steps.name: Playwright
steps.text: Hah, true enough.

steps.name: Playwright
steps.text: Yes, it was wonderful... Be it the film itself or otherwise.

steps.name: Shalem
steps.text: Lucian...

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Shalem
steps.text: Is he dead for good this time?

steps.name: Shalem
steps.text: Or is he still alive somehow?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: I'd have to think about that.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: But all you need to know, Shalem, is that you won't have to worry about shadows from the past invading your dreams—even when you're on Rhodes Island—ever again.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: And Playwright, you may write your scripts as you wish. About any topic, in any style.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: The Crimson Troupe is no more. You two are free.

steps.name: Playwright
steps.text: And you?

steps.name: Playwright
steps.text: You just said you'd have to think about his ending—which means you're stuck on that path, correct?

steps.name: Playwright
steps.text: 'Drama never dies'... So is the one sitting beside me right now no longer 'Blood Diamond', but 'Tragodia'?

steps.name: Shalem
steps.text: It sounds like you've paid a heavy price, Lucian.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: I wouldn't say so.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: If our previous attempts at escape or revenge were just scripts for us to follow, then now, we can finally step into the future.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: I will travel again, sing and perform again, until I am certain that what I create manages to match my joy and pain.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: It could be a new troupe or a new proposition, new adventures and new stories. Or, a more dazzling tomorrow, a more tragic truth...

steps.name: Playwright
steps.text: Hey, Shalem. We're all buddies here... would you like to lend him a hand?

steps.name: Shalem
steps.text: Lucian, a-are you sure about this?

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Those who've lost themselves in their haste. The ascetics who've closed off their senses and their selves. The laypeople who trudge through both highs and lows. And the creatures who chew on their pain.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: This land has never lacked for actors.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: ...So I welcome you both to join the 'troupe'.
